newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North silent on Canada iron ore rumour.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North silent on Canada iron ore rumour.

text.p: Australian miner North Ltd said on Tuesday it was looking for acquisitions but declined to comment on talk that it wanted to buy Iron Ore Co of Canada.

"I can't comment, I'm afraid, other than to say what we have been saying all along -- that we are on the look-out for opportunities in a range of commodities and iron ore is one of them," North spokesman Stewart Murrihy told Reuters.
Speculation that North was negotiating to buy a major stake in a Canadian iron ore producer first surfaced this month in local newspaper reports.
One stock analyst on Tuesday named the target company as the Iron Ore Co of Canada, one of that nation's major producers.
"It's a reasonable size, but not big in terms of the Australian context," the analyst told Reuters.
The analyst, who declined to be named, said North needed to find more long-term growth potential, but a move to buy the Iron Ore Co of Canada would not necessarily fit the bill.
"Basically its cost structure is not cheap," he said.
North produces a slightly low-grade iron ore from its huge Robe River mine in Western Australia and might be looking for a source of higher-quality iron ore, another analyst said.
The lower-grade fine iron ore and higher-grade lump iron ore are blended in steel-making, he added.
"If you can offer some high-quality Canadian lump, you can do a deal that allows you to sell more of Robe River (output) to a particular customer," he said.
North shares were trading at A$3.85 shortly before the end of trading, down nine cents on Friday's close.
The Iron Ore Co of Canada's major shareholders are Bethlehem Steel Corp, National Steel Corp, both of the United States, and Japan's Mitsubishi Corp.
